text.p: President Enterprises, Taiwan's biggest China investor, has accumulated losses of T$780 million from its mainland projects but expects to break even in 1997, a company spokesman said on Wednesday.

"The actual losses are lower than the figure reported to the Securities and Exchange Commission because the losses will be shared with some joint-venture partners," spokesman Yang Yu-pao said by telephone.
All Taiwan listed firms must report on overseas investments in their financial reports to the watchdog commission.
Yang attributed the losses to equipment purchases and personnel training in the early stages of investment projects.
"We expect to break even in 1997 and hopefully we will start seeing profits in 1998," he added.
President Enterprises has poured US$180 million into some 20 companies in China. Most of the ventures make food products.
The company has promised to invest up to US$200 million in China and its shareholders' meeting agreed in May to invest an additional US$100 million there.

However, heeding the Taiwan government's recent call to tone down economic links with China in a bid to avoid over-dependence on the mainland, President said in September it had abandoned a US$100 million power plant project in China.

Despite the China losses, President's overall operations saw a pre-tax profit jump a year-on-year 29 percent in the first 10 months to T$2.455 billion on sales of T$22.957 billion, according to figures issued on November 18.
